_comment: Corrections for rows that are wrong in the AccessMedicine source itself. Key = analyte name as produced by parse_lab_values; 'set' = fields of the Analyte model to overwrite (intervals as {lower_limit, upper_limit}); 'why' = the evidence. Applied before the factor consistency check, so a correction must make the row consistent with its own reference intervals.

Urea nitrogen (BUN).why: Source prints 0.0357, but its own intervals (8-23 mg/dL = 2.9-8.2 mmol/L) and the molar mass of urea nitrogen (2 x 14.007 g/mol -> 10/28.014 = 0.357) give 0.357.

Lamotrigine.why: Source prints μg/dL, but factor 3.91 = 1000/256.1 g/mol converts μg/mL to μmol/L, and 2.5-15 μg/mL is the therapeutic range.

Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase.why: Source prints U/mol Hb with factor 0.0645, but 1 U/g Hb x 64500 g/mol = 64500 U/mol Hb = 0.0645 MU/mol Hb.

Whole blood.why: The HbA1c row of the source carries its specimen ('Whole blood') as name because the group header is not indented. Factor 1 for '% of total Hb' -> 'Fraction of total Hb' is wrong: 4-5.6 % is 0.04-0.056 as a fraction, so the factor is 0.01 (as the source itself uses for methemoglobin).

Hemoglobin A2.why: Factor 1 for '% total Hb' -> 'Fraction of 1.0' is wrong: 2.0-3.5 % is 0.020-0.035 as a fraction, so the factor is 0.01.

Hemoglobin F (fetal hemoglobin in adult).why: Source prints the SI interval as '<2' although the unit is 'Fraction of total Hb' and the factor 0.01 is correct: <2 % is <0.02.
